topSignals.title: Elcogen reaches five and a half weeks quiet (39 days); Topsoe crosses the nine-week mark (64 days) — the whole tracked landscape went quiet today.
topSignals.text: Direct fetch of both priority-stack newsrooms confirms no solid-oxide-specific release since Elcogen's Sept 21 Metrosert cooperation item and Topsoe's Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset. A full sweep across all three tiers, the AI-datacenter deployment pipeline, regulation, competing on-site power, market/financials, research/IP, and the benchmark register today found no new item anywhere — the competitive landscape and SOFC_Benchmark_Records.md are unchanged from yesterday. Elcogen News | Topsoe press releases

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news-archive item since Sept 21 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed by direct fetch today — 39 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed by direct fetch today — 64 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by SAF/ammonia/e-methanol news, out of SOFC/SOEC scope.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation — new cycle, round 1 (FuelCell Energy, Mitsubishi Power): no new stack/cell-technology items for either. FuelCell Energy results repeated the already-logged Sept 2 Q3 FY2026 release (75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, $1.3B committed/$2.35B awarded backlog); Mitsubishi Power/MHI results repeated the already-logged 400 kW SOEC test module (confirmed dated April 2024).

Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": no new item; results recycled Bloom's Oct 23 Q3 2026 earnings and standing data-center-deal background, plus the standing Ceres H1 2026 interim results.

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation — cycle 5, round 3 (Plansee, Huatsing Power, Ningbo SOFCMAN, Chaozhou Three-Circle/CCTC, Delta Electronics, Shell), 7-day lookback: no new items for any of the six. Plansee results were powder-metallurgy interconnect background pages; Huatsing Power and Ningbo SOFCMAN results were academic/patent background only; Chaozhou Three-Circle (CCTC) again returned no company-specific SOFC/SOEC news (continuing open data gap); Delta Electronics results repeated the standing 2024 Ceres-Delta hydrogen-license deal; Shell results repeated the standing Ceres-Shell 10 MW SOEC demonstrator background.

Tier 3 sweeps — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR SK ecoplant" and "Doosan Fuel Cell OR Nexceris OR Watt Fuel Cell OR Kawasaki Heavy Industries": no new item for either sweep; results repeated the standing Sept 18 Doosan-Reverion $78M stack order, Convion's 2024 HD Hyundai acquisition history, SK ecoplant's 2023-vintage GDS Singapore story, and Nexceris's $60M SOEC scale-up deal.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway, hearing Dec 7), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B, Vineland NJ — first power block reported ready Oct 22; block capacity undisclosed; site not yet operational), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
